Map and MIDI details

    Movement advisories

    Conditional loading and cumulative exposure. These indicators inform review and preserve demanding choreography; they do not approve or reject maps.

    Model hypotheses

    Pose and recruitment remain unvalidated. Arm bars use muscle-force capacity; trunk and leg bars use lumped torque capacity. Scapular bars are heuristic. Isometric capacity is a diagnostic assumption.

    Exercise energy — experimental

    Experimental energy model: movement work plus activation/maintenance heat, using walking-derived coefficients. Unknown poses use an explicitly conditional mean-compatible extrapolation. Total includes a 1 MET baseline; active subtracts it. The time trace shows simulated demand. Menus, extra dancing, and post-exercise recovery are excluded. Sources and assumptions are in Evidence and uncertainty and the accompanying documentation.

    Assumed target-zone fit

    Assumed scoring-zone radii: 5 / 10 / 15 cm (2 / 3.9 / 5.9 in); these are unverified working values, not official hit thresholds. Targeting, bundles and scattered clusters are hypothetical strategies. These counts describe reconstructed paths, not actual player scores.

    Here and now

    Kinematic Analyzer For Synth Riders

    Choose your files, set up your player, then click Analyze map.

    1. Choose your files

    Start with the map you want to explore. You can choose another file before analyzing.

    No map selected

    Use an unencrypted .synth file provided by the mapper.

    No MIDI selected

    MIDI adds instrument lanes. To make one, upload your song’s audio to MuScriptor ↗ and select the downloaded MIDI here. The map’s audio offset is applied automatically.

    3. Analyze and explore

    When your files and player settings are ready, click Analyze map below. The progress window shows what’s happening.

    Then press Play, click a timeline to jump to a section, or select a muscle to follow its estimated effort. Use Unlock View to zoom, pan or turn the model; lock it again to scroll the page.

    Download your infographic or report from below the muscle graphs. Reopen Files & settings to change several settings before analyzing again.

    2. Choose your player

    Choose a difficulty and a player close to your size. Pick a movement style; optional settings can stay at their defaults.

    Optional measurements

    Use these to customize the player preset.

    Exercise-energy options

    The defaults give a model estimate. These choices change its assumptions.

    Advanced model settings

    Leave these at their defaults unless you want to compare modeling assumptions.

    Leave at zero unless the transcription needs a correction.
